propositions: A Jira issue's KEY changes when moved between projects; bindings keyed on the mutable KEY become stale when the issue's old key stops resolving (if third-party movers fail to update moved_issue_key table), causing the binding to silently detach and the local ticket to orphan from a live issue.

The fix additively captures the immutable numeric jira_id alongside the key on every binding; on a key lookup miss, the code re-asks by id and re-keys the binding to the issue's current key, updating the reverse index and treating the issue as present rather than absent.

The change is additive to avoid rewriting the shared Cloud binding store's identity semantics, the reverse index, or all jira_key-taking methods; existing key-keyed paths continue unchanged, and bindings predating this change (lacking jira_id) degrade safely with no fallback and no migration required.

On a moved issue where the old key returns 200 with the new key (via moved_issue_key table), the binding survives on the old key; only when moved_issue_key is not updated and the old key 404s does the id fallback re-establish the binding.

The absence probe must not retire an issue reachable by its recorded id; the reverse index must follow any re-key in the same operation; and the id fallback must not fire when the key still resolves normally (to avoid doubling absence probe cost).

Bindings written before this change (no jira_id) must continue working unchanged without migration, and Cloud behaviour must remain unchanged with no existing jira_key-taking method signature or semantics modified.
